entities.summary: Fort-de-France is a commune and the capital city of Martinique, an overseas department and region of France located in the Caribbean. This city, which had 76,512 inhabitants in 2019, concentrates major administrative, military, and cultural functions. It is also a significant economic, commercial, and port hub within the Lesser Antilles archipelago. The urban unit—that is, the agglomeration in the statistical and morphological sense defined by INSEE—had 115,501 inhabitants in 2022.
